newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks set record close level, banks soar.
newsitem.headline: French stocks set record close level, banks soar.

text.p: French stocks set a record closing level on Wednesday, 2.82 percent above the previous day's finish, after rising along with other bond and stock markets and getting added momentum from hectic speculation in French bank shares.
The blue-chip CAC-40 share index closed 82.40 points higher at 3,003.53 after setting an all-time high of 3,026.99 intraday.
Bank shares were set alight after Deutsche Bank said it could make an acquisition in France, with gains of up to 10 percent in individual stocks.
Bank stocks had started rising on Tuesday after news German Bayerische Vereinsbank and Bayerische Hypotheken-und Weschel-Bank AG said they planned to merge.

*BNP, most heavily traded in CAC-40, closes 10.14 percent up at 274.9 francs. Traders say it and Societe Generale gaining from view all bank shares due for upgrade and that those two banks are improbable takeover targets.

CCF seen as possible target among larger banks but some analysts say takeover speculation based on general optimism rather than specifics and that acquisitions could focus on privatisation candidates Credit Lyonnais or CIC.
*CAC-40 volume was a hefty 11.6 billion francs.

*Carmaker Renault, another big volume gainer, adds to Tuesday's advances to close up 8.62 percent at 179.0 francs after hitting year high of 187.8 intraday. Brokers say stock helped by stream of analysts' recommendations following winding down of Vilvoorde Belgian plant closure saga.
Recommendation changes also based on view that share appears undervalued veasus other rivals like Fiat and Volkswagen.
JP Morgan has set target of 185-195 francs for the stock, while Paribas Capital Markets analysts Francois Colli has set a goal of 200 francs and expects a profit from Renault this year.
*Peugeot also outperforms, closing up 4.58 percent at 616 francs.

*LVMH closes 4.30 percent higher at 1,626 francs. Group says it has 11.05 percent of Grand Metropolitan in its fight to turn a Guinness/GrandMet drinks merger into a three-way drinks tie-up with LVMH included.
